name: manual_f5a313
claim: When multiple agent sessions work the same infrastructure-critical fix concurrently (guard scripts, pre-push hooks, canonical-repo tooling), a shared append-only coordination board (this repo's GossipBus, queried via orchestrator.coordination.paths.canonical_db_path()) is what prevented duplicate/conflicting work across at least 4 concurrent agents on this single fix. The pattern that worked: post status BEFORE and AFTER any consequential step (not just at the end), read the board fresh before deciding next action rather than trusting your own last-known state, and treat the latest timestamped ruling as authoritative even when it contradicts an earlier instruction in the same thread -- rulings evolve as agents verify things live.

decisions.notes: Across this single ECC push-gate fix: an initial ownership-boundary mistake (hand-editing PT's manifest-managed files) was caught and redirected via a live board ruling; a code-review finding from a human/Codex on my first PR 311 commit was only visible because I re-checked the board before assuming next steps; and two follow-up bugs (linked-worktree scope, GIT_DIR leakage) were found and fixed by another agent entirely without any of us discovering the same bug independently or clobbering each other's commits. Zero force-pushes, zero --no-verify bypasses, zero lost work across the whole multi-agent sequence.
